title: Customer-facing throughput validation scenarios and load harness
creator: Ava Gomez
description: Purpose: deliver a repeatable, customer-facing throughput validation suite that operators and SEs can run during Dedicated onboarding and for SLA verification. This ticket defines the harness architecture, the measurement methodology (ramp, soak, sustain), acceptance scripts customers will run, and a reporting artifact that ties results back to autoscaling and fleet control behavior. The harness must exercise realistic prefix diversity, KV cache warmup determinism, and microburst patterns seen in production. It should be runnable both from our CI and as a customer-run script (containerized).
acceptance_criteria: Harness provides three canonical profiles (soak-steady, ramp-and-hold, stochastic-microburst) that can be parameterized by clients
Measured throughput (tokens/sec) and latency (p50/p95/p99) export to our metrics backend for post-run dashboards
Customer acceptance script produces a single signed report (JSON) with pass/fail for throughput SLOs and autoscaler behavior
Harness validates autoscaling did not exceed customer's reserved capacity unless configured to burst, and records any fallback model switches
Runbook and README published in Confluence and the onboarding scripts containerized in GitHub package registry
test_plan_steps: 1) Prepare: pin model version and deploy test instance in customer Dedicated cluster; ensure telemetry sink (prometheus pushgateway) reachable
2) Warmup: run deterministic KV-cache warmup using the synthetic prefix set for 10 minutes (warmup seeds documented below)
3) Ramp: increase RPS linearly to target over 2 minutes to avoid autoscaler hysteresis surprises
4) Sustain (soak): hold target for a configurable sustainment window (default 15 minutes) to measure steady-state throughput and tail latencies
5) Microburst: run stochastic microburst generator (short bursts with Poisson arrival) for 5 minutes to validate transient behavior and request queuing
6) Cooldown: ramp down and verify KV cache eviction and graceful resource release
7) Collect: pull telemetry, run post-processing script to compute tokens/sec, token-cost, p50/p95/p99 latencies, error-rates, and autoscaler events
8) Report: produce customer acceptance JSON and human-readable summary, upload to onboarding dashboard and attach to onboarding ticket
load_profiles: soak-steady: target_tokens_per_sec configurable, default 25k tokens/sec per pool; sustain 15m
stochastic-microburst: baseline 10% of target RPS with bursts up to 3x lasting 2-10s following exponential inter-arrival
kv-warmup-only: deterministic prefix replay to warm KV cache for reproducible latency baseline
pass_fail_thresholds: p99_latency: < 2.5x of committed SLA p99 (configurable per customer); default p99 < 1200ms
autoscaler: scale events must remain within reserved capacity corridor unless 'burst_enabled' is true
model_fallbacks: no unplanned model fallback events during soak

notes: Trade-offs: deterministic warmup improves repeatability but may not reflect unknown customer prefixes; mitigated by allowing optional 'customer_prefix_replay' mode.
Decision: measure tokens/sec instead of raw RPS because models with long generations can distort RPS-based capacity numbers.
Implementation detail: telemetry export will tag events with 'customer_id' and 'test_run_id' for isolation in dashboards.
Follow-up: add a configurable 'burst_budget' parameter to encode customer's reserved burst allowance and validate against billing metrics in a later ticket.
